qs.q: During respiratory examination, a patient has increased tactile fremitus and dullness to percussion over the right lower lung field. This suggests:
o: Right pleural effusion filled with fluid.
Right lower‑lobe pneumonia with alveolar consolidation.
Right pneumothorax with air in the pleural space.
Right lower‑lobe atelectasis causing volume loss.
qs.e: Consolidation transmits vibrations better (increased fremitus) and sounds dull to percussion.
